**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include second-read-only disagreements in resolver decisions**

When the maker already differs from the primary checker, this selection always chooses the primary checker, so fields disputed only by the independent second read are omitted from `governingComparison` and the resolver's required field set. This affects four committed rows (`qrow_9709_s17_qp_42_q05`, `qrow_9709_s17_qp_62_q05`, `qrow_9709_w17_qp_31_q06`, and `qrow_9709_w17_qp_33_q06`): their primary/second comparisons additionally dispute `owner_paths`, `node_roles`, `mark_ownership`, and `printed_marks`, but the resolver ledger decides only `layout_family_compatible`, silently staging unresolved structural disagreements.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the producer identity before certifying second reads**

When a file in a configured second-read directory was produced by the wrong worker, `validateLane` never compares `value.provenance.worker_id` or `value.provenance.shard_id` with the lane assignment and instead writes the configured identity into custody here. Such an output is therefore counted as an independent second read even if it came from the primary checker or another shard; the later verification only checks the selected checker against maker/resolver actors, not primary versus second-reader independence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify raw-response hashes before reporting them as valid**

If a checker extraction contains a stale or fabricated but well-formed `provenance.raw_response_sha256`, it still contributes to this `raw_hash_valid_count`: the import path validates the extraction file against the producer manifest but never reads or hashes the referenced raw response. Consequently the committed receipt certifies all 387 raw hashes without evidence for that claim, weakening deterministic custody and allowing an extraction to be disconnected from its alleged provider response.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the pre-resolution ledger before consuming it**

If the external pre-resolution ledger is changed or replaced after `prepare-resolver` writes the immutable resolver packets, finalization consumes the new bytes without checking a recorded hash or comparing each row with the packet's `frozen_pre_resolution_verification`. Neither the queue nor resolver manifest binds this ledger, and the reconstruction hash is created only after finalization, so a stale or modified ledger can change agreement staging or the maker/checker bases used to apply resolver outputs while all published custody artifacts still report success.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

This thread remains unresolved until the #1666 exact-head artifacts prove the repair.

The repair will locate and hash immutable raw-response bytes for every claim, fail closed for missing or mismatched custody, and rerun only genuinely unavailable candidate-blind checker reads. No hashes will be invented. This thread remains unresolved pending additive evidence.

This thread remains unresolved until that authority chain passes at the #1666 exact head.
